why.matters: Customers change segment, tier and region. Without history, last year's sales are silently re-attributed to this year's segment, and reports can't be reproduced.
why.failure: A customer moves from Bronze to Gold and every historical sale jumps into the Gold row: Gold looks like it grew 40% last year when nothing happened.
why.use: SCD type 2 (new row per change, valid-from/valid-to) for attributes people analyse over time; type 1 (overwrite) for corrections; surrogate keys so versions can coexist.
why.avoid: Type 2 on everything. Tracking history on phone numbers or typos bloats the dimension and confuses users.

verified.context: Kimball dimensional modeling techniques; portable SQL tested on SQLite in CI

asg.t: Build an SCD type 2 customer dimension
asg.brief: The CRM sends a change feed: one row per customer per effective change. Build dim_customer with full history so sales can be analysed by the segment and tier the customer had at the time.
req: A surrogate key, the natural key (CustomerID), the tracked attributes, ValidFrom, ValidTo and IsCurrent.
Don't create a new version when the CRM sends a "change" in which nothing tracked actually changed.
asg.exp: {{dw_change_rows|int}} feed rows → {{dw_duplicate_changes|int}} exact duplicate and {{dw_noop_changes|int}} no-op changes removed → {{dw_scd2_rows|int}} versions for {{dw_customers|int}} customers ({{dw_current_rows|int}} current, {{dw_historical_rows|int}} historical); {{dw_customers_with_history|int}} customers have more than one version.

asg.t: Which version was true on that day?
asg.brief: Attach each order to the customer version that was valid on the order date, so sales by tier reflect the tier at the time.
req: Point-in-time join: OrderDate >= ValidFrom AND OrderDate < ValidTo.
Decide, per attribute, whether it should be type 1 or type 2.
asg.exp: {{dw_example_customer}} has {{dw_example_versions|int}} versions: from {{dw_example_first_tier}} to {{dw_example_current_tier}}, latest change on {{dw_example_last_change}}. Orders before that date keep the earlier tier.

asg.t: Orders for customers who don't exist yet
asg.brief: Four orders arrived for customers the CRM hasn't sent yet. Last night's load dropped them because the join to dim_customer failed. Fix the design so no fact row is ever lost, and say what happens when the customer arrives later.
req: Never drop a fact row because a dimension row is missing.
Show which of the four orders can be resolved once the CRM catches up.
asg.exp: {{dw_early_orders|int}} early orders: {{dw_early_resolved|int}} resolve when their customer arrives (inferred members, updated later); {{dw_early_unknown|int}} never appears in the feed and stays on the Unknown member until someone investigates.

int.a: The natural key comes from the source (CustomerID). A surrogate key is a meaningless integer the warehouse assigns. With SCD type 2 one customer has several rows, so the natural key isn't unique; the surrogate key is, and facts point to the version valid at the time. Surrogate keys also protect you from source key changes and mixed sources.

Type 1 overwrites the attribute: history is lost, which is right for corrections (a misspelt name). Type 2 adds a new row with validity dates: history is kept, which is right for attributes analysed over time (segment, region, tier). Many dimensions mix both per column.

int.q: What is an unknown member and why add one?
int.a: A dimension row (often key -1, "Unknown") that facts point to when their dimension key is missing or invalid. Facts are never dropped, totals stay complete, and the unknown row makes data quality problems visible in reports.

Two names for the same situation: a fact references a dimension member the warehouse doesn't have yet. Create an inferred member (natural key only, attributes "pending"), point the fact to it, and update it when the real dimension row arrives.

ass.q: A customer changes from Bronze to Gold on 1 March. With SCD type 2, a February order is reported under:
ass.why: The fact points to the version valid on the order date.

ass.q: Why use a surrogate key instead of CustomerID in a type 2 dimension?
o: CustomerID isn't unique once a customer has several versions
ass.why: Each version needs its own key.

ass.q: In Power BI, relate FactSales to the type 2 dim_customer and build a matrix of sales by LoyaltyTier for 2025 and 2026. Then build the same with only the current version. Explain the difference to a sales manager.
ass.hint: Join facts on the surrogate key for history; use a separate "current customer" view (or the IsCurrent filter on a type 1 copy) for "as is today" analysis.
